faq.q: How can one person make a difference in the world?
faq.a: By choosing small, specific actions that help real people or places and repeating them. Consistent small acts add up and inspire others to join in.

faq.q: What can I do in one hour to help others?
faq.a: You can set up a small monthly donation, volunteer a local shift, volunteer remotely, write letters or cards, learn about one issue, review your spending, or check in on someone.

faq.q: Can I make a global impact without much money?
faq.a: Yes. Time, skills, attention, and kindness are valuable. Remote volunteering and advocacy cost little or nothing and can reach people far away.

faq.q: How do I choose a cause to support?
faq.a: Ask what breaks your heart, what you have experienced firsthand, and what skills you have. Personal causes are the ones people tend to stick with.

faq.q: How do I avoid burnout while helping others?
faq.a: Focus on one or two causes, give in amounts you can sustain, and treat giving as a steady habit rather than a single big push.

faq.q: Who said nobody need wait a single moment before starting to improve the world?
faq.a: Anne Frank wrote this line while in hiding during World War II.
